target_customer: Parents and gift-givers with kids roughly ages 4 to 11 who want a structured giving and volunteering activity at home
problem: Families want to teach children empathy and giving but lack ready-made, age-appropriate projects tied to real nonprofit partners.
business_model: Consumer subscription box delivered every other month, with a $5 donation per box directed by the child
product_category: Kids subscription box, education and giving

founders.name: Jessica Jackley
founders.background_notes: Per the YC company page. Also instructor of entrepreneurship at USC and author of Clay Water Brick.

technical_complexity.rationale: A physical subscription box with printed booklets, activities and an online giving page needs ordinary e-commerce and fulfillment work with no hard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: The nonprofit partnerships and founder profile helped, but kits, booklets and giving activities are easy to copy and the box format has no switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying it. Product Hunt lists KidPass, Thimble and Surprise Ride as alternatives, but only as a later listing.

market_need_then: Pandemic-era parents were buying subscription boxes and at-home learning products for kids, and 2021 parenting press covered giving-back boxes as a gift category. No hard demand metric was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and family-focused per the product description

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Entrepreneur, Motherly and Mom.com in 2021 and sold with a charity: water partner box, mostly through the founder's profile.

brand_strength.rationale: Press about the founder gave awareness, but no source shows a distinctive visual or community brand. The double L spelling is easy to confuse with Altruist-type names in search.

outcome_analysis: Alltruists launched in March 2021 on Product Hunt with a well-known founder and press coverage, but raised only a small YC-sized amount according to one database. The YC directory marks it inactive and calls the founder former, yet no shutdown post-mortem or news report was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty. A consumer box with bimonthly cadence and a one-person team likely struggled with acquisition cost, but that is not supported by a source.
notes: Funding rests on CB Insights only (about $130K total over 3 rounds, Seed II dated 2021-03-24, investors YC and Bali Venture Partners, the latter in one page only). Company website returned HTTP 503. Competitor list left empty because no source dated near March 2021 describes a direct volunteer box rival; For Purpose Kids and Little Loving Hands appear only in a November 2021 gift roundup and are not direct matches. Inactive status comes from the YC directory; cause and date not public.
